InCad for FreeCAD - what changed
================================

This build: VERSION
Newest build first. The build name is the name of the zip file.


0.8.0
-----
3D Line on a virtual cube, several work planes at once and turned with rings, Extrude Extents 2, Fillet Full, file pictures in Open, a Image tab, Screenshot, axes in assemblies; Sweep Wall and detached-Sweep fixes.

Improvements
- 3D Line (3D Model ▸ Sketch ▸ 3D Line): a line in space drawn on a virtual cube of points round the origin — its size
  and the step between the points are yours, written grey along its edges; nearer lines are thicker, far ones dotted,
  so the cube reads in space. Click a cube point, or anywhere on its lines (the point slides freely, grey numbers give
  the distances to the cube points either side); drag a point to move it. Lines, a Spline, or a spline Through the
  points, with a Curvature comb you can switch off. Sweep takes it as its path.
- Work Plane ▸ Offset ▸ Planes: several planes at once, 2×, 3×… the offset from the same base (for a loft); a new
  offset spaces them all, and each can still be moved on its own.
- Work Plane ▸ Turn (one compact row): X, Y, Z about the previous plane's axes or the global ones, typed or dragged on
  red, green and blue rings on the plane. The plane turns about its own point; the next one stays as it was.
- Extrude ▸ ⇄ 2: the second side has its own Extents 2 — Distance, To Next, Through All or To.
- Extrude ▸ To also reaches an edge or a work axis (through its middle), and follows it.
- Fillet ▸ Full beside the radius arrows: a full round between the two picked edges; off again, an ordinary fillet.
  Full Round Fillet has its own icon.
- File ▸ Open (and Import, Place in an assembly) shows a picture of the file under the pointer — a FreeCAD file's
  saved view, an STL, STEP or IGES drawn shaded — with its date and size, and Desktop, Documents, Downloads and the
  recent files' folders at the side.
- File ▸ Open lists only what opens: FreeCAD files, STEP and STL.
- Image tab: Insert Image (a JPG, PNG or BMP on the XY plane, 100 mm across), Scale / Transparency (click two
  points of the picture and type the real length between them — the whole picture scales, the first point staying put;
  a slider sets how see-through it is), On XY / XZ / YZ, Turn 90°, Mirror, Show / Hide. A double-click on the
  picture's row opens Scale / Transparency.
- View ▸ Screenshot (also in the File menu): the 3D view saved as PNG, JPEG or BMP at the screen's full resolution; a
  PNG can have a transparent background, for a web page.
- Assemblies show the axis of every turned body and hole (a cylinder or cone half way round or more) as a light dash-dot
  centre line; click one while Mate, Flush, Insert, Rotational, Slider, Cylindrical, Parallel, Perpendicular or Angle waits for a pick to
  use that axis.
- Image ▸ Scale / Transparency: Line ▸ Horizontal or Vertical turns the image about the first point so the line
  between the two points lies so; a magnifying glass beside the pointer while putting a point; the points are small
  and bright.
- 3D Line: a working layer — XY, XZ or YZ at the height you set (Tab / Shift+Tab or its arrows move it one step of the cube) — is bright
  and alone takes clicks, the rest of the cube a faint cage; switching layers goes through the last point. The 3D Line
  button is on the Sketch tab too (an open sketch is finished first).
- View ▸ Screenshot ▸ Screenshot (Window): the whole window — ribbon, browser, 3D view and status bar — as a picture.
  Make Assembly names each part file after its Solid and the assembly after the part + _assy; a new assembly saved on
  its first Place is named after that part + _assy.
- Assemblies: a part dragged by the mouse keeps its gizmo about 3 s (longer while the pointer is on a handle), so a
  handle can still be grabbed; the handle being dragged turns amber; the gizmo's arrow heads are smaller. Image ▸
  Scale / Transparency: the transparency slider no longer makes the image jerk; the magnifying glass shows the points
  as small crosses, not magnified.
- Tips are blue, errors red — in the dialogs and the status bar.
- Tools ▸ Material ▸ Appearance (also in a Solid's, a face's or the part's right-click menu): the picked faces or
  Solids — every Solid with nothing picked — in any colour, with a finish (Matte, Satin, Glossy, Metal, Chrome, Glass,
  Rubber), a texture over the colour (Brushed, Wood, Carbon, Knurl, Sand) and Hide Edges; shown as chosen, one Undo
  step. A coloured face keeps its colour when a feature moves it; assemblies show the parts' colours.

Bug fixes
- A Sweep's Wall came out uneven — thick on one side, thin on the other — when the profile's sketch was flipped on
  its plane (Reversed): the wall's inner outline was a mirror image of the outer one. Edit the Sweep and press OK to
  rebuild a wall made with the earlier version.
- A Sweep made away from the part, then picked in a dialog (Move Face…), was split off into its own Solid without its
  path sketch: FreeCAD repeated "links go out of the allowed scope", the dialog kept splitting it again and again and
  InnCad could crash. It now moves once, with its path (a Loft with its sections).


0.7.0
-----
Extrude To anything, Emboss round the corners, End of Part above sketches, Full Round Fillet, Show / Hide All Sketches.

Improvements
- Extrude ▸ To reaches any face of any Solid (flat or curved — a cylinder, a sphere), a work or origin plane, or any
  point (a corner, a sketch point, a work point: up to the plane through it parallel to the sketch). It follows the
  target when that moves.
- Emboss letters past the picked face run on round onto the faces that go on smoothly from it — the flat side and
  the rounded ends of a slot-shaped part, all the way round if need be — laid on them without stretching.
- End of Part can go above sketches, Texts and work planes too (it jumped back below them): they are greyed and
  hidden while below it, and come back when it goes down past them.
- Full Round Fillet (Fillet ▸ Full Round Fillet): pick the two parallel edges of a face — the end of a bar, a
  plate's side — and the face becomes a half cylinder that runs on into both sides.
- View ▸ Hide / Show ▸ Show All Sketches / Hide All Sketches: every sketch and Text of the part at once.
- Sketching on a plane inside the part makes the part see-through while the sketch is open, so the sketch shows.


0.6.0
-----
Compact ribbon, Work Plane on marked points, Section from a picked plane, slot Offset and Symmetric fixed.

Improvements
- Compact ribbon (View ▸ Ribbon Size ▸ Compact, also in ⚙): icons without names (the names are in the
  tooltips) and lower rows of small icons — the ribbon takes about 40% less height than Large.
- Work Plane ▸ Three points shows the same marked points as Section — corners, edge middles, circle centres on
  every shown Solid and the points of shown sketches — and takes three clicks on them. A corner of the part keeps
  the plane tied to it; an edge middle or circle centre places it there.
- Section builds the section from the selected flat face or plane, the XY / XZ / YZ planes from the browser
  too, with either face of the Section split button; a face or plane selected while sectioned moves the cut there.
- A constraint that repeats one the sketch has (Symmetric on a slot that is already Horizontal, Parallel on two
  Horizontal lines…) takes the older one off instead of breaking the sketch; the status line says which.

Bug fixes
- Offset of a slot (or any outline with smooth joins, like a rounded rectangle) gave "Sketch with redundant
  constraints" and the sketch stopped solving. The copy is now tied without repeats, by one offset dimension
  between two lines.
- Symmetric of a slot about an axis made the sketch fail (its Horizontal repeated the new constraint).
- Section on the XY, XZ or YZ plane cut nothing (the plane went far away). Section by 3 Points ignored a selected
  face or plane and showed its markers instead.
- The value box offered Centers / Overall / Gap for two concentric arcs or circles and failed when one was chosen.


0.5.5
-----
Construction switches only the selected lines.

Bug fixes
- Construction on a selected sketch line switched every line joined to it (the whole rectangle or
  polygon). Now only the selected lines switch; select several to switch them together.


0.5.4
-----
Emboss on a sphere, a Display Quality setting, and Revolve cut / Emboss fixes.

New features
- Emboss and Engrave on a sphere: the profile (a Text or any closed sketch, such as a star) is
  projected onto the sphere along the sketch's normal, on the side the sketch faces, and raised or
  cut along the radius. "Evenly round" is greyed out on a sphere. A profile that reaches past the
  sphere's outline, or past the edge of a cut-off sphere, is refused with a message.
- Settings (the gear at the top right) > Display Quality: Normal (faster) or Fine (smoother
  curves). Fine draws round faces with finer triangles, so a highlight on a ball or a fillet no
  longer shows facets. Default: Fine on a Mac, Normal on Windows. It changes only how the part is
  drawn: an open file is not marked as changed.

Bug fixes
- Emboss with a sketch that sits in another Solid (for example a star whose own Extrude was
  deleted) was made in that Solid, with nothing under it, so nothing appeared. It now goes on the
  Solid of the face you click, and the sketch moves there with it.
- A Revolve (or another feature) cancelled on a sketch area left a hidden copy of the area
  behind. That copy kept the sketch's projected edges construction, so a closed profile made from
  them could not be revolved or cut. The copy is now removed on Cancel (and on opening a file).
- Projected edges stayed construction when projecting took more than 6 seconds (several edges
  picked one by one); they now become normal geometry however long it takes.
- Construction on a projected edge now says what the edge is afterwards ("now normal: part of the
  profile" or "construction"): a projected edge looks the same either way.


0.5.3
-----
More speed, and a cleaner fillet preview.

New features
- Settings (the gear at the top right) > Show Log File: shows InCad.log, selected, in the Finder
  (and in the Explorer on Windows, where it sits in a hidden folder). Send it with a problem report.

Improvements
- A new or changed value (in any dialog, the value box, the Parameters panel) recomputes only the
  features that use it; it used to recompute the whole part. A Text on a part of 35 features took
  over a minute to place on a Mac; now it is instant, and so is Finish Sketch after it.
- Deleting a sketch or a feature no longer rebuilds the part from a Boolean onwards when nothing
  needs it (an unused sketch took 16 s on a part with a Boolean; now an instant). The same goes
  for everything that shows or hides features.
- Text and sketch patterns in an open sketch recompute only the sketch while you type; the part
  follows on Finish Sketch (each value took up to half a minute on a slow PC).
- The first change after opening a file with a Text no longer recomputes the Text and everything
  after it (FreeCAD marked every Text as changed on opening).
- Feature previews leave out the full geometry check (about a third of each preview); it runs once,
  on OK, and keeps the dialog open if something is wrong.
- Fillet, Chamfer and Move Face draw only the edges they make over the part, and only where the
  part does not hide them (an ellipse's seam and the far side of a ring showed through it).

Bug fixes
- A fillet preview outline that FreeCAD could not draw left an error in the log.


0.5.2
-----
Speed, and a slot's overall length.

New features
- Sketch > Dimension > Overall Dimension: click one edge of a slot (or two arcs or circles) and
  type its overall length, outer edge to outer edge. A new value makes the slot longer, not wider.
- The value box of a distance between two arcs or circles has three buttons: Centers, Overall and
  Gap (inner edges - what FreeCAD's Dimension gives on two arcs). A click switches the dimension;
  it keeps its name.

Improvements
- Big parts are much faster:
  - a click on a face of the part took up to a minute on a part with hundreds of faces; now it
    is instant, and so is the browser row lighting up the faces of its feature;
  - a whole recompute takes half the time on a part with a sketch's areas used in two solids;
  - editing an early feature: as in Inventor, the part is shown as of that feature while its
    dialog is open, and only that feature is recomputed as you type; the rest is recomputed once,
    on OK (each value typed used to recompute the whole part, and the dialog opened slowly);
  - a dimension changed in an open sketch recomputes only the sketch; the part follows on Finish
    Sketch;
  - a suppressed tapped hole no longer computes its modeled thread (3.6 s on every recompute);
  - Hole > Chamfer on a modeled thread is twice as fast.
- InCad.log starts every session with a line describing the computer, and names any InCad step
  slower than 0.1 s - send it with a report about slowness.


0.5.1
-----
New features
- File > Export... (Cmd-E): the part as STEP (.step / .stp) or STL (.stl, Normal / Fine).


0.5.0
-----
Text and Emboss.

New features
- Sketch > Text: words in a sketch that Extrude raises (Join) or engraves (Cut). Press Text (the
  cursor shows an orange Aa) and click two corners: a construction box is drawn and the text sits in
  it - Horizontal Left / Centre / Right, Vertical Top / Middle / Bottom, Fit to the box (the letters
  fill its width). Dimension or constrain the box and the text follows; a tilted box tilts the text.
  Or select a line or a circle first: the text runs along it (Start / Centre / End, Shift, Distance,
  Flip side). Font (the Mac's fonts), Bold, Italic, Size (the height of the capital letters), letter
  spacing, several lines. Mirror reads the text from the plane's other side. The text stays one
  object: double-click its row to change the words; it follows its box or curve at once while the
  sketch is open.
- 3D Model > Create > Emboss (Inventor's Emboss / Engrave): a Text or a sketch raised from or cut into
  a face. On a cylinder or a cone it is wrapped round the face (the letters keep their size, the
  height goes along the radius); on a flat face it goes straight. Around: As drawn, or Evenly round
  (the letters spread once round the whole face). Engrave may cut right through a thin wall (a
  stencil). It finds its face again when an earlier step changes.

Improvements
- Work planes, sketches and Texts made after the part's last feature show above End of Part (as in
  Inventor), not greyed out below it.
- The open sketch's Text is drawn as outlines on top (letters on a face no longer flicker into it).

Bug fixes
- A dialog that starts from its profile and still waits for a pick opens on that pick.


0.4.0
-----
Sketching, Move Face on round walls, and many fixes from testing.

New features
- Sketch > Offset is InCad's own now: one click on a line takes its whole shape (a rectangle, a
  polygon, a chain drawn line by line), the copy follows the pointer, a click places it. Corners stay
  sharp, a single line gives one parallel line (no more slot), a circle or ellipse gives a ring.
  One dimension drives the offset (Cmd-click adds more shapes, all at that distance).
- Sketch > Concentric (Constrain, after Coincident): click two circles, arcs or ellipses and their
  centres are tied.
- Move Face on round walls: a cylinder or an extruded ellipse / spline wall moves outward or inward
  by a distance (Step, Inventor or Together). One click takes the whole wall.
- Fillet / Chamfer: a click on a face takes all its edges (again: they come off); a click on an
  edge takes its smooth chain (a slot's lines and arcs, a ring in pieces).
- Circular Pattern: the axis can be any origin or work axis, a sketch line, a straight or circular
  edge, a round face, or two points clicked on the part. An axis through two points is drawn as an
  orange dashed line while the dialog is open (Revolve too).

Improvements
- While you pick, the dialog draws its result over the part as orange outlines: Fillet, Chamfer,
  Shell, Move Face and the others that show the part for picking.
- Sketch look: construction lines and shapes are orange, thinner and dashed with wider gaps;
  normal lines are a little bolder; in the dark theme the part is drawn darker while a sketch is
  open, so the sketch stands out. FreeCAD's green B-spline combs are hidden.
- Sketch ribbon: Spline is right after Line.
- Pattern along a path / Mirror in a sketch: a click on one side takes the whole shape.
- Extrude: several closed regions of a sketch are extruded together.
- Boolean: click order like Inventor - first the base (the solid that stays), then the tools.
- Threads Off / On: if some threads are on and some off, the first click turns all off, the next
  all on.
- Show All / Hide All Origin: every Solid's origin; when the origin is off screen the view zooms out
  to show it.
- Hole > Chamfer: the chamfered hole is shown (the plain hole was drawn on top of it).
- Move Face: a click near a corner picks the corner; Together follows curved walls; a chamfer or
  fillet picked with its face moves Together.
- Dimensions: a dead zone before FreeCAD's Dimension tool switches horizontal / vertical / aligned.
- No part open: the ribbon's first button is Start 2D Sketch (it makes the part).

Bug fixes
- FreeCAD hung after a Fillet on a big part (the edge picks re-selected themselves forever).
- Fillet / Chamfer: edges under a sketch's lines could not be picked; a sketch a feature uses is
  hidden; a pick on a sketch line takes the part's edge under it.
- A dialog whose window vanished (a Thread with a chamfer) blocked every command ("Finish the
  Thread dialog first"); now the next command cancels it. A dialog never stays open with dead
  buttons.
- Threads Off / On, section, measure and others failed on a part with a modelled thread
  ("undefined curve type").
- Construction / normal did not work on lines; a projected line switched to construction kept its
  colour.
- Stale "Area" faces of a cancelled region pick covered the part's edges.
- Closing a sketch while the Dimension tool ran crashed FreeCAD.
- Move Face: Together on a wall already moved Together, and flat faces that came back as B-splines.
- Hole > Chamfer on a modelled thread could come out invalid.


0.3.1
-----
Improvements
- Move Face: To also takes an edge that runs parallel to the faces (a level line, an arc, a circle)
  or a point (a corner, a work point); the faces move to its height and follow it if it moves. The
  edge or point may be on another Solid.


0.3.0
-----
Direct editing: Move Face.

New features
- New Move Face (3D Model > Modify, or right-click a face / the part): push or pull flat faces of the
  part without going back to the sketch. Pick one or more faces (they must face the same way), then
  a Distance (positive grows the part, negative cuts into it) or To a face or plane parallel to them;
  the faces move into that plane and follow it if it moves. Neighbours says what the faces next to
  the moved face do: Inventor (they keep their angle, a chamfer grows and the face gets narrower;
  holes stay holes), Step (only the face moves, a straight wall appears at a slanted neighbour's
  edge) or Together (the face and the chamfers / fillets next to it move as one piece).
- Move Face: an arrow stands on the face while the dialog is open. Drag it and the face moves with
  the preview; the Distance field follows and a label at the arrow shows the value. The arrow lights
  up under the pointer. Dragging replaces a formula or parameter in Distance with the dragged value
  in mm. With To it only shows where the face goes. Finish move on top of the right-click menu = OK.
  Distance starts at 0 mm (nothing moves until you type or drag).
- Move Face is a step in the history ("Move Face" in the browser): double-click to edit, Suppress or
  Delete like any feature; one OK is one undo step. It finds its faces again by their geometry, so
  it keeps working when an earlier feature is edited. When it cannot do the move it says why (a
  neighbour round across the move in Inventor mode, a move so large that a neighbouring face would
  vanish, a face that is no longer there, a face of another Solid) and changes nothing. Limits: flat
  faces only; in Inventor mode a neighbour that is round across the move cannot follow yet (use
  Step or Together).

Improvements
- Assembly: the gizmo arrows are a little smaller (the grab zone is as wide as before).


0.2.0
-----
Assemblies are ready to test in this build (they were untested in 0.1.x).

New features
- Assembly: drag a free part with the mouse. It moves only the way its constraints still let it
  (its own degrees of freedom); the other parts stay where they are, and a fully held part does not
  move. One drag is one undo step ("Move part").
- Assembly: click a free part to get its gizmo: an arrow for each direction it can slide, an arc for
  each axis it can turn about. Grab an arrow to slide the part, an arc to turn it. Handles are easy
  to catch (a wide grab zone on screen), the one under the pointer lights up, and the first arrow is
  up and down where the part can move that way. A click on empty space hides the gizmo.
- Assembly: each part's row in the browser shows "Grounded", "DOF n" (how many ways it can still
  move, counted against what holds it) or "DOF ?". View > Degrees of Freedom draws Inventor's DOF
  symbols on every free part; with it off, the part under the pointer shows its symbol as a tip.
- Assembly: new Parallel and Perpendicular constraints (faces or straight edges); Angle takes
  straight edges too.
- Assembly: Flip in the constraint dialogs: Mate and Flush (which way the faces face), Tangent
  (which side: outside or inside), Insert (direction), and the Rotational, Slider and Cylindrical
  joints. The preview turns the part over at once.
- Assembly: Tangent puts a round face outside the flat face's part by default.
- Assembly: the constraints in the browser (Relationships) have their own menu: Edit, Delete,
  Suppress / Unsuppress, Rename. Double-click a row to edit it. A suppressed constraint is struck
  through and its parts stay where they are. Constraint values are named after them (Mate1,
  Flush1 ...).
- Assembly: Edit on a part opens it in its own tab with the other parts of the assembly around it,
  grey and semi-transparent, at their real places (for reference only: they cannot be picked and
  are not saved). View > Assembly Context turns them off and on.
- Assembly: back in the assembly tab after editing a part, InCad asks before updating it; if you
  say no, the browser shows "Needs update" until you choose Update.
- Assembly: the browser shows each part's own history; double-click a part to open it. The part
  menu has Edit, Hide / Show, Suppress and Remove. Threads Off / On works on all parts at once.
- New Make Assembly (3D Model > Assemble, or right-click in the part): every separate piece of the
  part becomes a part file with its history, and a new assembly links them where they were (the
  largest grounded). Names are asked first; files go next to the part; the part itself stays as it
  was. Running it again offers "Replace existing files", so you don't get Train_2, Train_3 ...
- New Split (3D Model > Modify): the lines of a sketch become thin surfaces that cut the part. Keep
  all: every piece stays, each other piece as a Solid of its own (hide it, work on it, make it a
  part), still following the sketch; Keep picked: only the pieces you click stay.
- File > New Assembly in the menu. New remembers Part or Assembly; Tools > Ask on New brings the
  question back.
- Hide / Show works on Solids and assembly parts (also from their right-click menu in the browser);
  a hidden one is dimmed in the browser.
- Sketch: new Constraint List (ribbon Sketch > Constrain > List, or right-click in a sketch >
  Constraint List). It lists the sketch's constraints, including the ones with no icon to click
  (coincident points, point on a line). Pick a line or point to see only its own; select a row to
  see it in the sketch; check rows and press Delete selected (one undo step). Constraints that hold
  a sketch pattern, and dimensions used in a formula, are kept, and the window says why.
- Sketch: right-click a line or point to delete one of its constraints, or all of them.
- Sketch: projected edges are normal lines by default (as in Inventor), so they can be part of a
  profile right away. Construction switches them to construction and back. Old files follow the
  new rule in sketches nothing is built on yet.
- Hole: new Chamfer option for every hole (None / Start / Both ends, with a size): a 45° lead-in at
  the mouth of each hole and, for a through hole, at its exit. A tapped hole is chamfered from the
  thread's diameter, so a screw starts easily. With a seat (counterbore, countersink, spotface)
  only the exit can be chamfered.
- Boolean: new "Keep tool" option. Off (as it opens): the tool is used up and shows under the
  Boolean in the model tree. On: the tool stays a separate visible solid (print the pin and the box).
- Boolean: click anywhere on a solid to pick it as the base or a tool (the field names the solid,
  not the face clicked); a click on the base while picking tools is ignored. In an assembly the
  Combine button is now called Boolean too.
- Extrude: To Next goes toward the part when the default direction finds nothing; To accepts curved
  faces.
- Clearance fields say how they are measured: Boolean "Clearance (per side)", Thread and Hole
  "Print clearance (on diameter)".
- Dialogs: long choice lists wrap four buttons per row; choosing an option that needs a pick starts
  that pick, and a click on the field the dialog already made active keeps picking.

Bug fixes
- A new Solid sketched on another Solid's face took that whole Solid along with it (and Make
  Assembly then said the pieces could not be separated). It now holds only its own piece, and the
  Solid below stays shown. Older files are repaired when they are opened.
- Assembly: Mate and the other constraints picked in the 3D view sometimes lost which part a face
  belonged to, or said "can't be met" on parts placed far apart. Insert could move the grounded
  part.
- Assembly: Place asks for the part first (the save dialog for a new assembly looked like a part
  chooser).
- Delete on a Solid used by a Boolean broke the Boolean ("No source shape linked"); deleting the
  main Solid or a Split could make the other Solid vanish. Delete now asks and removes them
  together, and a pick on a piece deletes that Solid.
- A box drawn away from the part and split off into its own Solid no longer takes along what was
  built on the part after it, and sketches left on the part stay attached.
- Threads (Threads Off, Suppress) did nothing on a part with two threads when the second one was
  made after the first. Threads now attach to the hole itself; older files are repaired the first
  time threads are turned off.
- Threads Off / On left the modeled thread of a tapped Hole on (the button looked dead). It now turns
  those threads off too; the holes themselves stay.
- Threads Off / On (and Suppress on a thread) did nothing when something was made on a face of a
  later feature while the threads were off. InCad now finds the same face again by its geometry.
- Thread: choosing the Print-friendly standard sets the print clearance to 0.3 mm (0.2 mm for the
  others); a clearance you typed yourself is kept.
- Thread on a rod came out sloppy: a hair-thin fin (about 0.04 mm) stayed on every crest, worse
  when the rod was a little larger than the size (M2.5 on Ø2.594), and next to a shoulder. The rod
  is now turned down to the thread's crests first (a ThreadTrim step under the Thread); the end
  chamfers start from the part's own radius.
- Editing a thread: picks landed on the thread's own fill / bore / trim step instead of the part.
- Dialogs: a choice that becomes unavailable (after a new pick) moves to the next available one.
- Wireframe was nearly invisible in the dark theme. Its lines are now light (dark in the light
  theme) and thicker; Shaded puts the normal lines back. Switching no longer marks the file modified.
- Parameters lost their units in a file opened again (90 instead of 90°, 12 instead of 12 mm) in the
  Parameters list and in the dialogs; opening a file no longer marks its features for a recompute.


0.1.1
-----
Improvements
- Thread: any sensible size works in a hole. A Ø3 hole takes M3 (the hole is filled back to the
  M3 tap size first) or M4 (the hole is bored out to the M4 tap size first), always as a full,
  printable thread with the print clearance. The fill goes only where the hole has a wall all round,
  never into a crossing bore. A size far off the hole is still refused.
- Thread: Size "Auto" now picks the bolt that matches the hole (Ø3 -> M3, Ø4 -> M4); a tap-drill
  hole still gets its thread (Ø5.2 -> M6, Ø8.5 -> M10).
- New ribbon button "Threads" (3D Model > Modify): turns every thread off for faster work and
  redraws, and back on with a second click. A thread you turned off yourself stays off.
- Suppress / Unsuppress on a thread also turns off its chamfer and its fill or bore-out, so the
  part looks exactly as it did before the thread.

Bug fixes
- Thread on a through hole (or a rod free at both ends) started at the plain end, so the chamfered
  mouth had no thread when the thread was shorter than the hole. It now starts at the chamfered or
  rounded end.
- Thread: picking the front face as the Start face of a hole with a chamfered mouth said "The start
  face must be at one end of the threaded face". It is accepted now.
- Suppress / Unsuppress on a thread could fail with "ThreadProfile cannot be suppressed".


0.1.0
-----
First test build.
